_comment: How to answer each kind of text. 'order' decides which category leads when a text matches several (first wins). Each category: name, goal, approach, replies {match, playful, sincere} (lowercase on purpose, Gen Z texts lowercase), avoid. Stages and platforms add stage- and app-specific advice. All replies are suggestions to adapt, not scripts.

distress.name: Possible crisis
distress.goal: Make sure they're safe. Dating strategy doesn't matter here.
distress.approach: Ask directly and kindly whether they're okay. Don't joke it off. If they might be in danger, encourage them to reach out to someone now (in the US you can call or text 988; elsewhere, local emergency or crisis lines).

match: hey, i want to check, are you okay for real?
playful: not ignoring the joke but i'm gonna ask seriously. you good?
sincere: i care about you and that worried me. are you safe right now? i'm here and i'm not going anywhere
if it's heavy right now you can call or text 988 (us), i can stay on the phone with you while you do

avoid: Ignoring it or replying 'lol'
Making it about the relationship
Promising to keep it secret if they're in danger

red_flag_pressure.name: Pressure or control
red_flag_pressure.goal: Hold your boundary and see how they handle it.
red_flag_pressure.approach: You don't have to explain or bargain. State your line once, calmly. Someone worth keeping respects it the first time. If the pressure continues, that's your answer, and leaving is not 'ghosting'.

playful: guilt-tripping is not the rizz you think it is
sincere: i said no and i need that to be enough. if it's not, we're not a match
i'm not okay with being pushed on this. let's drop it

avoid: Over-explaining or apologising for your boundary
Giving in to keep them happy
Sending location, pictures or passwords because they insist

boundary.name: They set a boundary
boundary.goal: Make them feel safe. Respecting a limit is the most attractive thing you can do.
boundary.approach: Acknowledge it right away, without sulking or asking 'why'. Then keep the warmth going so they know the interest didn't depend on it.

match: of course, no rush at all
playful: say less. i'm still gonna be annoying in your texts tho
sincere: thank you for telling me. we go at whatever pace feels good for you
i'm into you either way, no pressure from me

avoid: Asking 'why not?' or bargaining
Going cold or dry right after
Joking about it in a way that makes them feel bad

dtr.name: Defining the relationship
dtr.goal: Give a clear answer. Ambiguity here is what turns talking stages into situationships or ghosting.
dtr.approach: If you feel the same, say so plainly, and suggest saying it properly in person. If you don't, be kind and honest now; dragging it out hurts more. Don't answer a heavy DTR text with only a joke.

match: i'm not talking to anyone else either
playful: locked in. no take backs
i was literally waiting for you to say that 😭
sincere: i really like you and i want this to be a thing. can we talk about it properly when i see you?
i've been feeling the same. i'm all in if you are

avoid: 'haha we'll see' (reads as no)
Leaving it on read to 'think'
Saying yes if you mean maybe
dtr.if_not_interested: i really like talking to you, but i'm not in the same place and i don't want to lead you on

exclusivity_probe.name: Testing the waters
exclusivity_probe.goal: Answer the real question underneath: 'am I the only one?'
exclusivity_probe.approach: Match their move with a small reveal of your own. If they deleted the apps, say whether you did too. If their friends ask about you, show you're happy about it.

match: wait same, i deleted mine last week
playful: tell them i'm amazing obviously
only busy with you lol
sincere: honestly i'm not really talking to anyone else. i like where this is going
i'd love to meet them

avoid: Ignoring the hint and changing topic
Bragging about other options to seem in demand
A dry 'lol nice'

physical_escalation.name: Getting physical (second base)
physical_escalation.goal: Move at a pace you both actually want, with consent that is clear, enthusiastic and ongoing.
physical_escalation.approach: If you're into it, say so and suggest a plan that's comfortable (a movie, cooking, a walk back to theirs). If you're not, a kind no or 'not yet' is enough. In person, check in ('is this okay?') rather than assuming. Agreeing to come over isn't agreeing to anything else, for either of you. Never send pictures you wouldn't be okay with being shared.

match: come over around 8? we can watch something
playful: only if i get to pick the movie
you're dangerous 😏 but yes
sincere: i'm really into you. i'd love to hang at yours, no pressure on anything
honestly i'd rather take it slow, but i still want to see you. dinner first?

avoid: Pushing after a 'not yet'
Treating 'come over' as a promise of anything
Sending or asking for nudes (risky, and illegal if anyone is under 18)
Going cold the day after getting physical; that's the #1 reason people feel used
physical_escalation.after_tip: The day after hooking up or a first kiss, text first. Something like 'had so much fun last night' prevents the 'was that all it was?' spiral.

love_bombing.name: Very intense, very early
love_bombing.goal: Enjoy it without getting swept up. Let actions catch up with words.
love_bombing.approach: Respond warmly but at your own pace. Watch for consistency over the next weeks: do plans happen, do they respect your time and your no?

playful: slow down, you haven't even seen me before coffee
sincere: i like you too, i just like getting to know someone slowly. let's keep going

avoid: Matching declarations you don't feel yet
Cutting off friends or plans because they want all your time

invite.name: They made a plan
invite.goal: Lock in the plan. A clear yes with a time is the best thing for a talking stage.
invite.approach: Say yes with specifics (day, time, place) or offer a counter-time. 'Maybe' without an alternative feels like rejection.

playful: say less. you're picking the place tho
only if there's food involved
sincere: i'd really like that. how's friday at 7?
can't do tonight but i really want to. are you free tomorrow?

avoid: 'maybe' or 'we'll see' with no counter-date
Taking hours to answer an invite
Saying yes then never confirming the time

soft_rejection.name: Soft no / fading
soft_rejection.goal: Find out where you stand without chasing.
soft_rejection.approach: Give them one easy opening to re-engage, then step back. If they want to see you, they'll suggest a time. Don't double-text a soft no. Matching their energy protects your dignity and keeps the door open.

match: all good! hope things calm down
playful: valid. you know where to find me
sincere: totally get it. if you want to hang when things settle, let me know
no pressure at all. i'd like to see you again, but only if you're feeling it too

avoid: Several texts in a row asking what's wrong
Guilt-tripping ('you always say that')
Pretending you don't care with a cold 'k'

jealousy_test.name: A little jealous
jealousy_test.approach: A quick, light explanation plus some attention back to them. Treat it as a sign they care. If it becomes demanding or controlling, see the red-flag advice.

match: nah i was with my roommates
playful: are you jealous? 👀 that's cute
sincere: she's just a friend. you're the one i'm texting

avoid: Making them more jealous on purpose
A long defensive paragraph

vulnerable.name: Opening up
vulnerable.goal: Be someone safe to talk to.
vulnerable.approach: Lead with care, not solutions. Ask what they need: to vent, a distraction, or a plan. Follow up later ('how are you feeling today?'). This builds more closeness than any flirt.

playful: want me to send you the dumbest tiktoks i have until you laugh
sincere: i'm here. do you want to vent or do you want a distraction?
proud of you for getting through today. want to call?

avoid: Turning it to your own problems
Jumping to advice they didn't ask for
A one-word reply

compliment.name: They complimented you
compliment.goal: Receive it, enjoy it, and give something back.
compliment.approach: Don't deflect ('no i'm not'). Accept it with some personality, and compliment back about something specific.

playful: i know 😌 but tell me more
ok you're making me blush and i'm in public
sincere: that genuinely made my day. you're really easy to talk to too

avoid: Deflecting or putting yourself down
Only 'lol ty'

flirt_tease.name: Flirting / banter
flirt_tease.goal: Keep the push-pull going and raise the heat a little.
flirt_tease.approach: Tease back with confidence; match their energy and add a little. Mix in one sincere line every so often so it doesn't stay surface-level forever.

playful: careful, i might actually start liking you
is this your way of flirting? because it's working
sincere: ok but for real i like talking to you

avoid: Getting defensive at a tease
Over-the-top sexual replies to light flirting
Dropping a dry 'lol'

soft_launch_care.name: Getting closer
soft_launch_care.goal: Show the care back. This is the routine-building phase before it gets official.
soft_launch_care.approach: Mirror the routine (gm/gn, 'home safe', sharing things). Use 'we' back. Bring up something specific from your recent chats to show you were listening.

playful: you're stuck with me now
sincere: honestly the best part of my day is talking to you

avoid: Going dry when they get affectionate
Pulling back because it's 'too fast' without saying so

apology_late.name: Sorry for the late reply
apology_late.goal: Make it easy to pick the conversation back up.
apology_late.approach: Brush it off lightly, don't keep score, and give them something to answer.

match: no worries! how was your day?
playful: i'll allow it. this time
sincere: don't stress, life happens. how are you doing?

avoid: Passive-aggressive 'it's fine 🙂'
Making them wait the same amount of time on purpose

reengage.name: Back after a silence
reengage.goal: Find out if they're back for real before you invest again.
reengage.approach: Be friendly but don't pick up at full intensity. If they ghosted before, you can name it lightly. Real interest shows up as a plan or consistent texting, not one 'hey stranger'.

match: hey! long time. how've you been?
playful: oh so you DO remember my number
sincere: good to hear from you. honestly i was a bit confused when you went quiet. what's been up?

avoid: Acting like nothing happened if it hurt you
Instantly going back to daily texting

meme_share.name: Shared something with you
meme_share.goal: React and turn it into a conversation.
meme_share.approach: React genuinely (😭 or 'this is so us'), then add something: your own story, a callback or a related send. Leaving shares unanswered is a quiet ghosting signal.

playful: you're not allowed to know me this well
ok now i have to send you one back
sincere: i love that you thought of me with this

avoid: Just hearting it with no reply, over and over
Leaving it on opened

question_back.name: They're curious about you
question_back.goal: Answer with substance, then ask back.
question_back.approach: Give a real answer with one detail they can latch onto, then ask a question back. That's the loop that keeps a talking stage alive. Fill in the [your answer] bits with something true and specific.

playful: that's classified. trade you for yours
sincere: good question, [your answer]. what about you?

avoid: Answering without asking anything back
One-word answers

enthusiastic.name: Excited
enthusiastic.approach: Bring the same or a little more energy. Excitement that gets a flat reply is how people feel 'too much' and pull back.

playful: ok we're both unwell about this and i love it
sincere: i love how excited you get about stuff

avoid: A flat 'cool' or 'nice'

checkin.name: Low-effort check-in
checkin.goal: Turn a 'hey' or 'wyd' into a real conversation.
checkin.approach: Answer with something specific, add a hook (a question or a tease) and, if it's going well, a soft invite. Don't mirror their low effort with a 'nm hbu'.

match: rotting in bed watching tiktoks. you?
playful: thinking about how you owe me a coffee
was literally about to text you
sincere: hey you, how was your day?

avoid: 'nm u?' (dry for dry kills it)
Ignoring it because it was low effort

dry.name: Dry reply
dry.goal: Figure out whether it's a bad moment or fading interest, without chasing.
dry.approach: One dry reply is noise; three in a row is a pattern. Give one good opening (a question or a plan). If that also gets a one-word answer, step back and let them come to you.

playful: wow the enthusiasm 😭
ok i'll let you go, you're clearly busy
sincere: you seem a bit off today, everything okay?
no stress if you're busy, text me later

avoid: Sending three paragraphs to a 'k'
Calling them a dry texter after one reply
Matching with a dry reply back (two dry texters = the chat dies)

statement.name: General message
statement.goal: Keep the conversation easy and moving.
statement.approach: React to what they said, add a bit of yourself, and leave a hook: a question, a tease or a callback.

playful: ok that's actually iconic
sincere: tell me more about that

avoid: Ending with nothing to answer

closing.name: Wrapping up
closing.goal: End on a high note so the next chat starts easy.
closing.approach: Close warmly and leave a thread for next time (a callback, a plan, or 'tell me how X goes'). Ending on a good note is what makes them want to text first next time.

playful: ok bye, miss me
sincere: talk later! good luck with [thing they mentioned]

avoid: Trying to drag the chat on after they've said bye
Ending on a dry 'k'

threat.name: Threat
threat.goal: Stay safe. This isn't a conversation to win.
threat.approach: Don't argue, bargain or send anything they ask for. Screenshot the messages (with their username showing), then block and report them in the app. If they threaten to share pictures of you: don't pay and don't send more; StopNCII.org (adults) or Take It Down (under 18) can get images blocked across apps. Tell someone you trust, and if you feel in danger, contact the police (911 in the US).

match: i'm not doing this. blocking you now.
sincere: stop contacting me. i've saved these messages.

avoid: Replying with threats of your own
Paying, sending more pictures or meeting up to 'sort it out'
Deleting the messages before you've saved them
Dealing with it alone

hostile.name: Insult or abuse
hostile.goal: Don't take the bait. Protect your peace.
hostile.approach: You don't owe a reply. If you answer, make it one calm line, then stop: arguing gives them what they want. If it keeps happening, mute, block or report them, and screenshot anything you might need later. Someone who's into you doesn't talk to you like this.

match: ok, i'm done with this conversation
not talking to you like this
sincere: that's not okay. if you can't talk to me with respect, i'm out
i'm not going to argue. bye.

avoid: Insulting them back: it escalates, and they'll screenshot yours
Over-explaining or defending yourself
Staying in a chat that keeps making you feel small

negging.name: Backhanded compliment
negging.approach: A compliment with a put-down attached is meant to make you try harder for them. Don't thank it and don't try to prove yourself. If it keeps happening, that's who they are.

playful: was that supposed to be a compliment
sincere: that came off kinda rude ngl

avoid: Trying harder to impress them
Thanking them for it
Laughing it off when it keeps happening

roast.name: Roasting you
roast.goal: Keep the banter fun, not hurtful.
roast.approach: With a laugh or emoji attached, an insult is usually teasing, and teasing is affection between people who get on. Roast back lightly if it's mutual. If it actually stung, you can say so.

playful: you're lucky i like you
ok that was rude but funny
sincere: lol ok that one kinda stung ngl

avoid: Going for something they're really insecure about
Pretending it doesn't hurt when it keeps happening

talking.name: Talking stage
talking.about: Getting to know each other with romantic intent, no label. Lots of 'wyd', questions, memes and first plans.
do: Ask follow-up questions and remember the answers
Move from DMs to text or Snap, then to a real plan within a week or two
Text at a steady rhythm instead of all-or-nothing
dont: Let it run for months without meeting up
Play the 'wait twice as long' game
Interview them; share about yourself too
ghost_risks: No plan after 1-2 weeks of texting

flirting.name: Flirting stage
flirting.about: Compliments, teasing, emojis like 😏🙈😳, 'you're trouble', banter that feels charged.
do: Tease back and raise the heat a little at a time
Give a sincere line now and then
dont: Jump to explicit content when the flirting is light
ghost_risks: Compliments but no interest in seeing you

second_base.name: Getting physical
second_base.about: Kissing and making out, invites to come over, 'can't stop thinking about last night'. Physical intimacy before (or alongside) defining things.
do: Talk about pace and comfort openly; check in during
Text the next day so it doesn't feel like that's all it was
dont: Assume a 'come over' or past kiss means yes to more
Send or ask for intimate pictures
ghost_risks: Texts that only happen when they want to hook up
Going cold right after getting physical
No plans that aren't at someone's place

dtr.name: About to be official
dtr.about: Good-morning/good-night routines, 'we' language, meeting friends, deleted apps, 'are we locked in?'
do: Answer 'what are we' clearly and kindly
Have the official talk in person
Mirror the care: gm/gn, 'home safe', inside jokes
dont: Keep the apps if you said you're exclusive
ghost_risks: Dodging 'what are we' more than once
One person still using the apps

situationship.name: Situationship
situationship.about: Acting like a couple without the label, often for too long. 'Not looking for anything serious', on-and-off texting.
do: Decide what you want and say it
Set a time limit for yourself
dont: Wait for them to 'come around' indefinitely
ghost_risks: They're clear they don't want more

fading.name: Fading
fading.about: Short replies, long gaps, no questions, vague 'maybe's. Often how ghosting starts.
do: Give one clear opening, then step back
If you're the one losing interest, say so instead of ghosting
dont: Read it as a test you need to pass
ghost_risks: Three dry replies in a row
Left on read or opened for days

snapchat.name: Snapchat
notes: Streaks are low-effort daily contact; a streak alone isn't deep interest
'Opened' with no reply for hours = low priority right now
Chatting (not just snapping) and sending selfies (not just the ceiling) = real interest
Moving from Snap to text or FaceTime is a step up

instagram.name: Instagram DMs
notes: Story replies are a low-risk opener; reacting to every story is a crush signal
Only story-watching, no texting = possible orbiting
Sharing reels to you = thinking of you
'Seen' with no reply reads like left on read

tiktok.name: TikTok DMs
notes: Sending TikToks daily is a love language; react, don't just like
Reposting 'relationship' TikToks after talking to you can be a soft hint

imessage.name: iMessage / SMS
notes: Read receipts on + no reply hits harder
Tapbacks (❤️, 😂) on a question is a soft dodge
Moving to texting from apps means more trust

whatsapp.name: WhatsApp
notes: Blue ticks with no reply = left on read
Voice notes mean they're comfortable with you

dating_app.name: Hinge / Tinder / Bumble
notes: Move to a date or another app within a few days, chats on apps die fast
Asking for your number or Snap = interest
Deleting the app is a big exclusivity signal

discord.name: Discord
notes: Inviting you into VC or a small server is like meeting friends
Gaming together counts as quality time

generations._comment: Markers that suggest how someone texts. A rough guess from style only; never treat it as anyone's actual age.

typing._comment: Meanings for typing-style signals the analyzer measures (not word lists).

period_end.label: Ends with a period
period_end.meaning: To Gen Z a full stop on a short text ('ok.', 'sure.') reads cold, annoyed or serious.

all_lower.label: All lowercase
all_lower.meaning: Normal, relaxed Gen Z texting. Nothing negative.

all_caps.label: ALL CAPS
all_caps.meaning: Excitement or yelling-for-fun, not anger (in Gen Z texting).

stretched.label: Stretched letters
stretched.meaning: 'heyyy', 'stoppp', 'okayyy': extra letters add warmth and energy. More letters, more flirty.

keysmash.label: Keysmash
keysmash.meaning: 'asdfghjkl' means overwhelmed, flustered, or laughing too hard to type.

multi_question.label: Lots of questions
multi_question.meaning: They're curious about you. Very good sign.

question.label: Asks a question
question.meaning: Gives you something to answer, keeps it going.

no_question_short.label: Short, no question
no_question_short.meaning: Nothing to reply to. If it keeps happening, they may be winding down.

long.label: Long message
long.meaning: They put real effort and thought into this one.

ellipsis.label: Trailing dots ...
ellipsis.meaning: Hesitation, awkwardness, or something left unsaid. Gen Z can read it as passive-aggressive.

lol_softener.label: 'lol' as a cushion
lol_softener.meaning: A 'lol' tacked onto a serious line softens it. They mean the line; the lol is protection.

burst.label: Several texts in a row
burst.meaning: Double/triple texting: comfortable and engaged, not playing the waiting game.

slow_reply.label: Slow reply
slow_reply.meaning: A long gap before answering. On its own it could be life; as a trend it's a fading signal.

fast_reply.label: Quick reply
fast_reply.meaning: They answered fast. They were waiting on you or happy to talk.

shorter_than_you.label: Much shorter than your text
shorter_than_you.meaning: You wrote a lot and got a little back. One-sided effort is the classic early ghosting sign.

random_emoji.label: Random emoji
random_emoji.meaning: A string of unrelated emoji reads as decoration, not a message, so this reading goes by the words.

tone_groups._comment: Emoji whose tones fall in three or more of these groups are mixed at random.
